tagline: Because the record must not forget.
cov_lead: Where this record looks, and whether its claims can be re-checked. Sakshi records a case only where it has a source; a state with no source is a declared gap, not an absence of crime.
cov_framing_title: What this record can, and cannot, be
cov_framing: "Every case in India" is not reachable, and this record does not claim it. The NCRB recorded roughly 29,500 rape cases and 68,000 POCSO cases in 2024 — and the NCRB counts only cases that reached the police; media covers a fraction of those, and many assaults are never reported at all. What Sakshi can honestly claim is narrower and still worth building: every case that appears in an accessible public source, with the gaps published. This page is that accounting — where we look, and where we do not yet.
cov_trackable_note: "Days without justice" is only honest if a case's status can be looked up again. A record is trackable when it carries a court anchor — a CNR, or a year-qualified FIR (station + number). Media-only records are not. This fraction is the record's re-checkability, and it is why court-record sourcing matters.
landing_lead: A civic-accountability record of publicly reported sexual-assault cases across India, compiled from public judicial records and credible media.
recent_lead: The latest published cases across all states, newest first. Each links to its full record and cited sources.
recent_empty: No recent cases to show yet. New cases appear here as they are published, each cited to its public source.
verified_hint: Independently re-checked against its cited source by a second AI review.
status_changed_hint: When a material fact of this case (status, court, charges or accused) last actually changed. Re-checks that found no change are not shown.
explore_lead: Filter by state, status, year and more. Every view is a shareable link.
no_results_hint: Try clearing a filter or widening the year.
genesis_text: No cases have been published yet. Sakshi is live and awaiting its first daily update — published cases will appear here, each cited to its public source.
select_state: Select a state to see its cases.
sources_identifying_summary: More sources (web address may reveal withheld details)
sources_identifying_note: The web address of these sources may itself state a detail this record withholds by law (such as a victim's age or gender). We link the publisher, not the headline. Open only if needed.
tier_media: Reported in media — not yet traced to a court record
traced_to_court: Traced to a court record on
traced_to_court_hint: This case was first seen in the media and has since been matched to an official court record.
severity_hint: Severity is derived from the public charge sections — it describes the offence, not any person.
scale_this_week: cases entered the record this week
scale_cumulative: cases on the record in total
scale_heat_label: Daily intake over the recent window.
jur_lead: How each district's cases are moving — sortable. Pendency (median and longest) is shown only for cases with a queryable court anchor whose status can be re-checked; where that column is empty, no case here is yet trackable — see the Coverage page.
jur_coverage_disclaimer: Ranking is meaningful only AMONG covered jurisdictions. A district with more cases here may simply be better covered by our sources, not more dangerous — this is a record of PUBLICLY REPORTED cases, not a crime rate. A state with no source of its own is marked; its counts are floors, likely undercounts.
jur_no_source_hint: No state-specific source feeds this jurisdiction yet — cases here are surfaced only incidentally, so the count is a floor. See the Coverage page.
offenders_lead: Names appear only from official court records, never from media. Every accused is presumed innocent; acquittals and quashals are shown with equal prominence.
offenders_empty: No court-recorded offenders yet — names appear only from official court records.
accused_withheld: Withheld (media-sourced, not yet in court record)
presumption_banner: An accused person is presumed innocent until proven guilty. Status shown reflects public court records as of the last update.
disclaimer: Sakshi is a civic-accountability record of publicly reported cases, compiled from public judicial records and credible media. It is NOT a crime-rate statistic and not a substitute for official data such as the NCRB: a case appears only where Sakshi has a source, coverage is partial (see the Coverage page for the states sourced and the declared gaps), and reporting rates vary across regions and time. A larger count reflects more sourcing or more reporting, never simply more crime.
